topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
target_audience: University students with basic programming/math background

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/math background

sections.title: The Problem: Context Blindness
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of reading a long sentence where words depend on previous words (Recurrent Neural Networks). Show how old methods lose context over long distances.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The bank of the river is muddy,' the word 'bank' is ambiguous. A simple model forgets 'river' by the time it reaches 'bank'.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Query, Key, and Value (QKV)
sections.content: Explain the retrieval system analogy. Query (what I want), Key (what I offer), Value (the actual information). Use a graphical 'Library Catalog' analogy.
sections.example: Think of a student (Query) searching for a book in a library. The book spine label is the 'Key', and the content inside the book is the 'Value'.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Calculating Attention Scores
sections.content: Visualizing the Dot Product. Explain that we multiply the Query by the Key to find how much 'attention' word A should pay to word B. Use a heatmap animation.
sections.example: In 'The cat sat on the mat because it was tired,' calculate the attention scores: 'it' has a high dot-product match with 'cat' (the subject) vs. 'mat' (the object).

sections.title: Softmax and Weighting
sections.content: Convert raw scores into probabilities (0-1 range) using Softmax. This ensures the model 'distributes' attention across all words intelligently.
sections.example: Visualizing a 'Spotlight' beam moving across words. 'it' puts 80% of its spotlight on 'cat' and 20% on 'mat' to resolve ambiguity.

sections.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
sections.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough. We run multiple attention layers in parallel to capture different types of relationships (e.g., grammatical vs. semantic).
sections.example: Like having one editor check for grammar (Head 1) while another checks for the emotional tone of the story (Head 2), combining results for a complete understanding.

storyboard.title: The Problem: Context Blindness
lecture_lines: Context is hard for simple models to maintain.
'The bank' needs 'river' to be understood.
Old models forget context over long distances.
animations: Fade in text "Query", "Key", "Value" at top of screen with color #FFFFFF.
Display a central vector representation and animate Query approaching it with color #FF5733.
Animate Key vector aligning with Query, changing to color #33FF57.
Animate Value vector being weighted by the alignment score with color #3357FF.
Fade out all elements to transition to the final concept with color #888888.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Query, Key, and Value (QKV)
lecture_lines: We use a library catalog analogy for retrieval.
Query is what you want to find.
Key is the label on the shelf.
Value is the content inside the book.
QKV enables intelligent information lookup.
animations: Fade in Q, K, and V matrices with distinct colors #FF5733, #33FF57, and #3357FF.
Highlight Q and K matrices individually to emphasize their role with color #FFFF00.
Simulate the matrix multiplication Q*K^T with a bright flash effect in color #FFFFFF.

storyboard.title: The Mechanism: Calculating Attention Scores
lecture_lines: Dot product measures similarity between two vectors.
Query multiplied by Key gives raw attention scores.
High scores mean more focus on that word.
'It' pays attention to 'cat' over 'mat'.
This creates our attention heatmap.
animations: Display the attention score formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(dk))V with color #FFFFFF.
Flash the term QK^T / sqrt(dk) to emphasize scaling with color #FF5733.
Show the transformation process of scores into probabilities with color #33FF57.
Visually map the probabilities to weighted Values with color #3357FF.
Consolidate the entire process into a single block with color #CCCCCC.

storyboard.title: Softmax and Weighting
lecture_lines: Scores can be large and unmanageable.
Softmax maps scores to a zero-one range.
Attention becomes a probability distribution.
The spotlight highlights relevant words clearly.
Weights sum up to one perfectly.
animations: Fade in the score vector with values [2, 1, -1] in color #FFFFFF.
Apply Softmax to the vector, showing the values transition to probabilities with color #FF5733.
Visualize the final weights being applied to the Value matrix with color #33FF57.

storyboard.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
lecture_lines: One attention head is rarely enough.
Parallel heads capture different types of relationships.
One head tracks grammar, another tracks tone.
Combining heads provides a complete understanding.
Multi-head attention mimics human cognition.
animations: Split screen into four smaller regions for different heads with color #FFFFFF.
Animate each head performing its own attention calculation in colors #FF5733, #33FF57, #3357FF, #FFFF33.
Show the results of each head being concatenated together with color #FFFFFF.
Project the concatenated output into the final representation vector with color #CCCCCC.
Final display highlighting the combined result across all heads with color #FFFFFF.
